verification_policy: These records are sourced from the structured research corpus and remain partially_verified until acquisition, mechanics, and CaC availability are independently reconciled against canonical in-game evidence.
audit_note: Negative Ultimate Finish claims were removed because the checked research records do not carry explicit evidence establishing that an Ultimate Finish is not required. Unresolved cases remain null.

records.name: Absolute Zero
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 96 "The Shadow Dragons"; research corpus reports a 28% Ultimate Finish reward slot. Also listed in TP Medal Shop rotations.
records.skill_description: A stationary contact-counter aura that freezes an enemy who makes melee contact during the active window.
records.mechanics_notes: The source describes this as a counter rather than a movement evasive: the user remains in place while melee contact triggers a freeze. Ranged attacks do not trigger it. Freeze duration is disputed after balance changes; older text and current community testing disagree, so no fixed duration is treated as canonical.
records.combo_notes: A successful freeze can create a follow-up opportunity, but the reported post-nerf duration is short and a follow-up hit can knock the target away.
records.pve_notes: The contact counter can punish close-range AI pressure and swarms, but its stationary activation and stamina cost make timing important.
records.pvp_notes: The audible activation cue and melee-only trigger give opponents counterplay; exact current frame windows remain unverified.

records.name: Acid
records.unlock_method: Not obtainable by normal player progression; research corpus identifies it as an enemy-only skill with no player-facing shop or acquisition entry.
records.skill_description: A short-range corrosive spit attack used by Saibaman-type enemies.
records.mechanics_notes: The research corpus identifies separate internal NPC variants and no player acquisition metadata. It describes a simple single-hit Ki attack with no documented damage-over-time effect; Poison is a separate skill.
records.combo_notes: Not a normal player skill, so player combo routing does not apply.
records.pve_notes: Relevant primarily as an enemy attack encountered in quests; it is documented to prevent players from mistaking NPC data for an obtainable skill.
records.pvp_notes: Not documented as a normal player-usable skill; no player PvP routing is assigned.

records.name: Afterimage Strike
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 81 "Wake Up!"; research corpus reports a 30% reward on a normal clear. Also listed in TP Medal Shop rotations.
records.skill_description: A temporary self-buff that uses afterimages to automatically evade incoming attacks and allows immediate attacks after the evasive movement.
records.mechanics_notes: The source describes an active defensive window of roughly 10–15 seconds based on community timing. Incoming melee and Ki attacks can whiff automatically without the user spending stamina for each dodge. Throws and some tracking Ultimates can still interact with the move after balance changes. Exact current duration and exception list are not independently verified.
records.combo_notes: The ability to attack immediately after an automatic dodge allows the opponent's whiff to become a combo starter.
records.pve_notes: The automatic evasion can be especially effective against predictable AI pressure in PQs and Expert Missions.
records.pvp_notes: The defensive buff creates strong pressure reversal opportunities, while predictable activation, throws, and certain tracking attacks provide counterplay.

records.name: Android Kick
records.unlock_method: Skill Shop after completing the "Android Warfare" story saga; research corpus lists a 5,000 Zeni price. Also listed in TP Medal Shop rotations.
records.source_quest_or_shop: Skill Shop after Android Warfare; TP Medal Shop rotations
records.skill_description: A somersault Strike with a second input that either performs a dive kick or retreats with a backflip.
records.mechanics_notes: The research source describes two branches from the same startup: a follow-up input produces a dive kick, while holding back produces a backward flip instead. The source reports approximately 10% community-measured damage for the attacking branch.
records.combo_notes: The attack branch can extend pressure while the retreat branch provides a feint/disengage from the same startup animation.
records.pve_notes: Useful as an inexpensive early-to-mid progression Strike option, although its branching behavior may be less valuable against predictable AI.
records.pvp_notes: The shared startup can make the attack/retreat choice a mix-up, but exact frame data is not established.

records.name: Android Rush
records.unlock_method: Android 16 Instructor Quest 3; research corpus identifies it as a mentor-training reward rather than a shop or PQ drop.
records.skill_description: A four-hit rushing Strike whose final knockback direction can be selected with the left stick.
records.mechanics_notes: The source describes three kicks followed by a backhand launcher. The final direction is steerable: neutral sends the target forward, up-stick produces a downward spike, and down-stick produces an upward launch. The research source reports community training damage around 1,829, not an official multiplier.
records.combo_notes: The selectable ender can route into forward carry, ground-bounce style follow-ups, or aerial extensions depending on the chosen direction.
records.pve_notes: The controllable knockback direction can help keep enemies positioned for follow-ups and is useful when managing multi-target encounters.
records.pvp_notes: The selectable ender gives a Strike build more control over combo routing, though exact hit-confirm and timing requirements remain unverified.
